title: `PopupMenu` search doesn't prioritize/sort exact matches
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.beta [e06dd8106e4c9113f2a3b20e4ceef16f3e85735e]

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta (e06dd8106) - Fedora Linux 43 (Forty Three) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Single-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

The fuzzy search added to `PopupMenu` in #117958 does not sort or otherwise prioritize the matches with a higher `FuzzySearchResult::score` (beyond culling the ones with a score that's zero or less), which means that in a list of mostly similar items, typing in a search query that exactly matches one of the items won't necessarily bring that anywhere near the top, forcing you to scroll for it anyway.

I'm framing this as a discussion because it's not obvious to me what the fix would be.

It might be that sorting the results is the correct thing to do, but that might not always be desirable, so should in that case be configurable.

Another option is to expose the fuzzy search parameters (i.e. `allow_subsequences` and `max_misses`), to make the results less lenient, and thus allow more to be filtered out.

However, even with `allow_subsequences` set to `false` and `max_misses` at `0` a query of `i t e m` will still match with `item`, so it might be that we should allow truly disabling fuzzy search in favor of a simple substring filter.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the MRP main scene
2. Right-click anywhere
3. Type in "Item 41" in the search field
4. Note how nothing gets filtered out
5. Note how "Item 41" doesn't bubble up to the top in any way

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[popup-menu-fuzzy-ordering.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27237749/popup-menu-fuzzy-ordering.zip)
